title: Latency percentile — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, a reviewer asks what p95 means. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences defining the percentile, contrasting it with the average, and naming who experiences the tail.

vocabulary.meaning: reading a latency figure as the value below which a stated share of requests fall, rather than as a typical value
the slowest share of requests, which a mean hides and which is experienced by real users rather than by nobody

expectedElements: The percentile is defined in terms of a share of requests
The contrast with the average is explicit
The affected users are described, not abstracted away
modelAnswer: The ninety-fifth percentile is the value below which ninety-five percent of requests fall over the stated window; it is neither the maximum nor a typical value. We track it instead of the average because a small share of very slow requests barely moves a mean, so the mean can look healthy while some users wait seconds. The evidence that this share matters is our own volume: five percent of our traffic is a few thousand requests a day. Those users experience the tail and retry.
commonMistakes: Explaining the percentile as an average or as a maximum
Describing the tail as a statistical artefact rather than as affected users
variants: Rewrite the update to justify adding a higher percentile to the dashboard.
